Generating final model predictions after relativizing

Alice Stears

2026-06-18

In this document, we integrate our forest classification model as well as models for each different functional group and ecoregion we considered into CONUS-wide predictions of both absolute and relative cover. We show maps of these model predictions that are generated using contemporary climate, weather, and soils data, and assess how these predictions compare to observed data using maps of residuals, quantile plots, bias, and RMSE. We also show model predictions of both absolute and relative cover made using modeled climate and weather data from the end of the 20th century under RCP 8.5. We used data from two different generalized circulation models (GCMs) from CMIP5: “BNU-ESM”, a cooler and wetter model, and “IPSL-CM5A-MR (France)”, a hotter and drier model. For these future predictions of cover, we display maps that show how these future model predictions compare to modeled contemporary cover. We present all of this information (maps of contemporary cover predictions, residuals, quantile plots, RMSE, bias, and maps of future cover based on GCMs) for both absolute and relative cover.

## function to maek predictionss f
makePredictions <- function(predictionDF, modelObject, scale  = TRUE) {
  ##
  # predictionDF <- climDatPred
  # modelObject <- bestLambdaMod_grassShrub_totalHerb
  # # ##
  # predictionDF = modDat_quantile,
  # modelObject = forb_CONUS, scale = FALSE
  # 
  # pretend to scale the input variables so the model object can predict accurately
  if(scale == TRUE) {
  predictionDF <- predictionDF %>% 
  mutate(across(all_of(prednames), base::scale,scale = FALSE, center = FALSE)) 
  }
  # modelPredictions
  modelPreds <- predict(object = modelObject, newdata = predictionDF, type = "response")
  # add predictions back into the input data.frame
  predictionDF <- predictionDF %>% 
    cbind(modelPreds)
  
  # truncate all predictions to max out at 100 
  #predictionDF[predictionDF$modelPreds>100 & !is.na(predictionDF$modelPreds),"modelPreds"] <- 100
predictionDF[predictionDF$modelPreds < 0 & !is.na(predictionDF$modelPreds),"modelPreds"] <- 0

  # print predicted data
 return(predictionDF)
}

# custom functions for plotting inset figures
            # make function to add inset
           get_inset <- function(df) {
              p <- ggplot(data = df) +
             facet_wrap(~lyr, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
                geom_density(aes(Cover)) +
                theme_bw(base_size=9) +  ## makes everything smaller
                theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill="transparent"),  ## white plot background
                      panel.border = element_blank(),
          axis.title.y = element_blank(),
          axis.title.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size=rel(2)), ## tiny axis text
          axis.text.y = element_text(size=rel(2)), ## tiny axis text
          axis.line.x = element_line(size = .5),
          axis.line.y = element_line(size = .5),
          panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          plot.background = element_blank(),
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_blank()) 
  return(p)
           }

{

        geom = ggplot2:::GeomCustomAnn,
        inherit.aes = TRUE, params = list(grob = grob,
                                          xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax,
                                          ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax))
           }

First, we show predictions from the model of forest classification

These maps show predictions of forest classification using contemporary and modeled future climate data, where the predicted value is the forest classification. We arrive at these classification values by translating the continuous probability of forest that was predicted by a binomial generalized linear model to binary values using a cutoff of 0.382 (values greater than 0.382 are forest, while values less than or equal to 0.382 are not forest). This threshold is derived from the average prevalence of forest in the data used to fit the binomial model. Note that while the climate data used in model predictions is either contemporary or from GCMs, the soils data used is static across time.

# read in model
forestMod <- fit_glm_bestLambda <- readRDS("./models/yesOrNoTrees_bestLambdaGLM_10.rds")
# get threshold for making predictions binary
best_threshold_bestLambda <- readRDS( "./models/ForestModelPrevalence.rds")

## print out model statement
coefficientTable <- data.frame(coefficients(forestMod))
responseVar <- "P(forest)"
coefficientTable$coefficientName <- rownames(coefficientTable)
coefficientTable$coefficients.forestMod. <- round(coefficientTable$coefficients.forestMod., 6)
  
  # print out coefficients w/ coefficient names
tempNames <- paste0(
  apply(coefficientTable, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x) {
    if (x["coefficientName"] == "(Intercept)") {
      paste0(x["coefficients.forestMod."])
    } else {  
      paste0(x["coefficients.forestMod."], "*", x["coefficientName"])
    }
    }
  ),
  collapse = " + "
)

# print the unscaled model statement
  unscaledModelName <- paste0(responseVar, "~ 1/ (1 + exp(-(", tempNames,")))")
#print(unscaledModelName)

  mutate(pred =  as.numeric(1/ (1 + exp(
    -(3.38565522 + -0.79822221*((tmean - 10.6678425) / 5.14823079) +  4.74536062*((prcp - 767.94900623) / 506.45362111) + -0.49798680*((prcpTempCorr - -0.02007952) / 0.40677333) +  0.22745494*((isothermality - 36.51862827) / 5.41402375) + -0.39051271*((clay - 17.45502795) / 8.23327615) +  0.53857137*((coarse - 11.18397843) / 11.24234211) + -0.40059849*((AWHC - 14.91029339) / 5.4856826) + -0.83406990*I(((prcp - 767.94900623) / 506.45362111)^2) + -0.94850342*I(((prcpTempCorr - -0.02007952) / 0.40677333)^2) +  0.19450621*I(((isothermality - 36.51862827) / 5.41402375)^2) + -0.04772718*I(((clay - 17.45502795) / 8.23327615)^2) + -0.26519959*I(((coarse - 11.18397843) / 11.24234211)^2) +  0.07438930*I(((AWHC - 14.91029339) / 5.4856826)^2) + -0.29049829*((prcp - 767.94900623) / 506.45362111)*((isothermality - 36.51862827) / 5.41402375) + -0.16800569*((tmean - 10.6678425) / 5.14823079)*((isothermality - 36.51862827) / 5.41402375) +  0.07625545*((tmean - 10.6678425) / 5.14823079)*((prcp - 767.94900623) / 506.45362111) + -0.55536190*((tmean - 10.6678425) / 5.14823079)*((prcpTempCorr - -0.02007952) / 0.40677333) + -0.37720980*((clay - 17.45502795) / 8.23327615)*((AWHC - 14.91029339) / 5.4856826)
      )
                                        )
    )))

 # mutate(pred_interp = replace(pred_interp, list = pred < 0.136147, 0)) %>% 
   mutate(pred_binary = pred,
    pred_binary = replace(pred_binary, pred_binary > best_threshold_bestLambda, 1), # now, make the interpolated continuous model predictions binary
         pred_binary = replace(pred_binary, pred_binary <= best_threshold_bestLambda, 0)) 
# now, translate the continuous predictions to correspond to the 'buffer zone' that we want to use (currently best_threshold_bestLambda +/- 0.1) to come up with weighted predictions around the transition from forest to non-forest
# make an interpolation function
interpFun_forest <- stats::approxfun(x = c(0, 0.3216, best_threshold_bestLambda, 0.6213, 1), # values we're interpolating *from*
          y =c(0, 0, 0.5, 1, 1), # what we're interpolation to (desired values at the end)
          method = "linear")
preds_byHand <- preds_byHand %>% 
  mutate(pred_contNew = interpFun_forest(pred))

Below is a map of the ‘scaling factor’ that we use to make predictions of total tree cover CONUS-wide. If the model-predicted probability of forest is high or low, then we take the predictions of total tree cover for forest and non-forest at face value. However, if the model predicted forest probability is near the threshold for making the predictions binary, we interpolate the continuous P(Forest) predictions within this buffer to generate a continuous “scaling factor” that we use to mix the predictions of total tree cover from the forest and non-forest model together.

         #drop_na(paste(response)) %>% 
  #slice_sample(n = 5e4) %>%
  terra::vect(#geom = c("Lon", "Lat")
    ) %>% 
  terra::set.crs(crs(test_rastTemp)) %>% 
  terra::rasterize(y = test_rastTemp, 
                   field = "pred_contNew", 
                   fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE) 
# get the extent of this particular raster, and crop≠ it accordingly
plotObs_2 <- plotObs %>% 
  crop(ext(min(tempExt[,1]), max(tempExt[,1]),
           min(tempExt[,2]), max(tempExt[,2])) 
       )

map_ecoRegion_current_Transformed<- ggplot() +
geom_spatraster(data = plotObs_2, maxcell = 5e+10) + 
  geom_sf(data=cropped_states %>% st_transform(crs = st_crs(test_rast)) %>% st_crop(st_bbox(plotObs_2)) ,fill=NA ) +
 xlim(-2150000, 2510000) +
 ylim(-2005000, 1000000) +
  coord_sf(datum = st_crs(test_rastTemp)) +
 scale_fill_gradientn(
                                             colors = c("wheat", "orange", "purple", "forestgreen"),
                                             values = c(0, 1e-10, 0.99999, 1),
                                             limits = c(0,1),
                                             na.value = "lightgrey"
                                             ) +
             theme(
                   axis.text = element_blank(),
                   strip.text = element_text(size = 15),
                   title = element_text(size = 18),
                   axis.ticks = element_blank()) + 
labs(title = c("Scaling factor for tree cover, based on contemporary dayMet data (2023)"),
     subtitle = c("Values are the average binary predictions \nwithin each 1 km x 1 km grid cell"), x = "", y = ""
     )

Now, we show the predictions from the model that predicts whether a location has no trees. These predictions are combined with the predictions from the forest model, such that only locations that the forest model predicts to be un-forested can then be predicted to be un-treed.

# read in the model object
# we use the oneSELambda model, since the predictions are very similar to the best lambda model
zeroTreeMod <- readRDS("./models/yesOrNoTrees_oneSELambdaGLM_10.rds")
# get threshold for making model predictions binary
zeroTreeMod_threshold <- readRDS("./models/yesOrNoTreeModel_ModelPrevalence.rds")

# predict w/ contemporary data
preds_byHand <- preds_byHand %>% 
  mutate(zeroTree_pred = predict(object = zeroTreeMod, climDatPred, type = "response"),
         zeroTree_binary = zeroTree_pred) %>% 
  # make predictions of zero tree binary
  mutate(zeroTree_binary = replace(zeroTree_binary, zeroTree_binary > zeroTreeMod_threshold, 1), 
         zeroTree_binary = replace(zeroTree_binary, zeroTree_binary <= zeroTreeMod_threshold, 0)) %>% 
  # now, get predictions for locations that the forest model predicts to be forested
  mutate(zeroTree_nonForest = zeroTree_binary) %>% 
  mutate(zeroTree_nonForest = replace(zeroTree_nonForest, pred_binary == 1, NA))

# predict w/ future 1 data
preds_future1_byHand <- preds_future1_byHand %>% 
  mutate(zeroTree_pred = predict(object = zeroTreeMod, forecastClimSoilsDatPred_1, type = "response"),
         zeroTree_binary = zeroTree_pred) %>% 
  mutate(zeroTree_binary = replace(zeroTree_binary, zeroTree_binary > zeroTreeMod_threshold, 1), 
         zeroTree_binary = replace(zeroTree_binary, zeroTree_binary <= zeroTreeMod_threshold, 0)) %>% 
  # now, get predictions for locations that the forest model predicts to be forested
  mutate(zeroTree_nonForest = zeroTree_binary) %>% 
  mutate(zeroTree_nonForest = replace(zeroTree_nonForest, pred_binary == 1, NA))


# predict w/ future 2 data
preds_future2_byHand <- preds_future2_byHand %>% 
  mutate(zeroTree_pred = predict(object = zeroTreeMod, forecastClimSoilsDatPred_2, type = "response"),
         zeroTree_binary = zeroTree_pred) %>% 
  mutate(zeroTree_binary = replace(zeroTree_binary, zeroTree_binary > zeroTreeMod_threshold, 1), 
         zeroTree_binary = replace(zeroTree_binary, zeroTree_binary <= zeroTreeMod_threshold, 0)) %>% 
  # now, get predictions for locations that the forest model predicts to be forested
  mutate(zeroTree_nonForest = zeroTree_binary) %>% 
  mutate(zeroTree_nonForest = replace(zeroTree_nonForest, pred_binary == 1, NA))

                   field = "zeroTree_nonForest", 
                   fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE) 
# get the extent of this particular raster, and crop≠ it accordingly

  crop(ext(min(tempExt[,1]), max(tempExt[,1]),

geom_spatraster(data = plotObs_2, maxcell = 5e+10) + 
  geom_sf(data=cropped_states %>% st_transform(crs = st_crs(test_rast)) %>% st_crop(st_bbox(plotObs_2)) ,fill=NA ) +
 xlim(-2150000, 2510000) +
 ylim(-2005000, 1000000) +
  coord_sf(datum = st_crs(test_rastTemp)) +
 scale_fill_gradientn(
                                             colors = c("wheat", "forestgreen"),
                                             values = c(0, 1),
                                             limits = c(0,1),
                                             na.value = "lightgrey"
                                             ) +
             theme(
                   axis.text = element_blank(),
                   strip.text = element_text(size = 15),
                   title = element_text(size = 18),
                   axis.ticks = element_blank()) + 
labs(title = c("Locations with no trees, based on the zero tree model,\n--using future climate data from the BNU-ESM model"),
     subtitle = c("Values are the average binary predictions \nwithin each 1 km x 1 km grid cell"), x = "", y = ""
     )
